name: Wet meadow
notes: Seasonally saturated grassland without standing water: tufted grasses, rushes and sedges with a tall wildflower layer (meadowsweet, joe-pye weed, marsh marigold) and scattered willow; drawn on European water meadows and Molinia grasslands and the North American sedge meadows.

shrub.silhouette: grey-green rounded bush of many stems

growth.juvenile_note: Germinates within a day on wet mud: two tiny round cotyledons, then a downy shoot with small obovate, dull grey-green leaves (grey-hairy beneath). Branches low into a rounded, dense, many-stemmed bush; twigs downy, with raised ridges under the peeled bark. Fallen or broken stems root where they touch wet ground.
growth.source: Stace, New Flora of the British Isles, and Meikle, Willows and Poplars of GB and Ireland (BSBI) for form, 4-10 (15) m size and phenology; USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Salix (willow seed has no dormancy and germinates within 12-24 h on wet ground (USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Salix)); growth rate, first seed and lifespan estimated for a fast, short-lived sallow

fruiting.source: Stace and Meikle (BSBI): catkins before the leaves in Mar-Apr, males 2-3 cm with yellow anthers ('pussy willow'), females grey-green; hairy flask-shaped capsules 7-10 mm shed seed May-June; key early food for bumblebee queens and honeybees; fruit set and crop estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Seed needs a winter's cold before sprouting; the seedling has two small round cotyledons, then whorls of 3-5 lance-shaped toothed leaves on a short upright stem. The first year it stays a knee-high leafy shoot; from year 2 the clump sends up several stout purple-spotted stems 1-2 m tall topped by flat domes of mauve flower heads.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Eutrochium maculatum: to 2 m, rose-purple heads of 8-22 disc florets, butterflies and bees, open wetlands); standard native-seed guidance (cold-moist stratification before spring germination). Ages estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (late-summer flat-topped clusters of rose-purple heads with 8-22 disc florets and no rays; butterflies and honeybees; larval host of several moths). Plumed achenes, timings and counts estimated from Eupatorieae.

growth.juvenile_note: Small epigeal seedling; the first leaves are simple and 3-lobed, soon followed by a basal rosette of pinnate leaves with a large 3-5-lobed toothed end leaflet, dark green above and whitish beneath. From a creeping rootstock it builds a clump, and from year 2-3 sends up tall, stiff, reddish stems crowned by frothy cream flower plumes.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Filipendula ulmaria: stems 1-2 m, cream flowers early summer to early autumn in irregular cymes, visited mainly by flies; damp meadows, fens, wet woods); Grime et al. Comparative Plant Ecology (wetland perennial, spring germination). Ages estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (dense irregular cymes of small cream 5-petalled flowers with 7-20 stamens, strongly scented, visited mainly by flies); floras (each flower gives 5-10 small spirally twisted one-seeded fruits, water-dispersed). Timings and counts estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: A slender seedling tuft of flat, soft, mid-green leaves. Over a few years its tillers pack into a firm tussock with swollen, bulb-like leaf bases that store food; the leaves turn straw-buff and die back each autumn, so the tussock is pale all winter. Narrow purple-tinged panicles rise on tall bare stems in late summer; on wet moors old tussocks become raised pedestals.
growth.source: Wikipedia (dense tussocks to 120 cm, flowers Jul-Sept, moist heath, bogs and moorland, pH 3.5-5); Taylor, Rowland & Jones 2001 Biological Flora of the British Isles: Molinia caerulea (J. Ecol. 89) for deciduous habit, storage leaf bases and tussock formation; ages estimated
